title: Rotating Filament in Orion B: Do Cores Inherit Their Angular Momentum from Their Parent Filament?
question: Do cores inherit their angular momentum from their parent filament, and what is the specific angular momentum profile of a star-forming filament in LBS 23?

data.arrays: 12 m, 7 m, and Total Power (TP) arrays
data.sensitivity: 32 mJy beam^-1 per 0.08 km s^-1 channel (N2D+); 0.54 mJy beam^-1 (continuum)

what.value: YSO catalog (HOPS Class 0, Class I, flat-spectrum sources and Spitzer-identified sources)

evidence.quote: The HOPS Class 0, Class I and flat-spectrum sources are marked by cyan circles, cyan triangles and cyan stars, respectively (Furlan et al. 2016).

The Spitzer-identified pre-main sequence star and red protostar (detection in 24 _µ_ m without detection in 4.5, 5.8 or 8 _µ_ m) are marked as a black star and cross, respectively (Megeath et al. 2012).

external_data.citation: Furlan et al. 2016; Megeath et al. 2012

recipe.goal: Fit N2D+(3-2) hyperfine spectra to derive system velocity and velocity dispersion maps
recipe.method: Model the brightest 25 hyperfine components of N2D+(3-2) with 25 Gaussians using known relative frequencies and intensities
key_parameters: 25 hyperfine components from Table 2 of Gerin et al. (2001)

recipe.goal: Derive H2 column density map, number density, mass, and N2D+ abundance of the central filament
recipe.method: Convert Herschel-Planck 850 um optical depth to N(H2), correlate with smoothed ALMA TP N2D+ integrated intensity to derive a linear empirical relation, apply to high-resolution N2D+ moment 0 map, and compute N(N2D+) assuming optically thin LTE
key_parameters: V_lsr integration range 8.4 to 11.3 km s^-1; smoothed resolution 36.0''; 4 sigma threshold on Moment 0 map; central filament dimensions 13.8'' x 87.6'' (5540 x 16640 AU)
assumptions: gamma_OrionB = 3460 mag, delta_OrionB = -0.001 mag, A_V/A_K = 8.933, N(H2)/A_V = 0.93 x 10^21 cm^-2 mag^-1, cylindrical geometry with average depth = r * pi / 2, T_ex = 10 K, mu = 1.37 (for M(H2) in Eq. A3)

recipe.goal: Fit radial column density profile and compute moment of inertia, rotational energy, and gravitational energy
recipe.method: Rotate map by 11 deg, average radial H2 column density profile perpendicular to the filament over a 0.18 pc region, fit a Plummer-like profile, and integrate analytically to obtain moment of inertia I, rotational energy E_rot, gravitational energy E_G, and beta_rot
key_parameters: Rotation angle 11 deg north of east; averaging length 0.18 pc; R = 2770 au; L ~ 34,000 AU
assumptions: Inclination i = 0 deg (plane of sky); mean molecular weight mu = 2.33

recipe.goal: Measure filament rotation, specific angular momentum profile, and gravitational stability
recipe.method: Extract average radial velocity profile across minor axis, compute rotation velocity, angular frequency, critical linear mass (for non-rotating and rotating isothermal cylinders), total specific angular momentum J = I*omega/M, and radial profile j(r) = r * |V(r) - V_c|
key_parameters: V_c = 10.05 km s^-1 at r = 0; central density rho_0 = 3.0 x 10^-17 g cm^-3; dimensionless truncation radius x = 3.0
assumptions: Isothermal rotating cylinder in hydrostatic equilibrium at T = 10 K

recipe.goal: Calculate non-thermal velocity dispersion, Mach number, turbulent energy, and dissipation rate
recipe.method: Subtract thermal velocity dispersion of N2D+ in quadrature from observed velocity dispersion in outflow-free region to get sigma_NT, Mach number M_s, turbulent energy E_sigma = M * sigma_NT^2, and dissipation rate L_sigma = E_sigma / t_diss
key_parameters: Average sigma_v = 0.20 km s^-1 in outflow-free region; cylinder aspect ratio A = 6; eta = 5
assumptions: T_g = 10 K, mean molecular weight mu = 2.33, c_s = 0.19 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Estimate plane-of-sky magnetic field strength and magnetic energy
recipe.method: Apply Chandrasekhar-Fermi method using JCMT SCUBA polarization angle dispersion and ALMA C18O(2-1) density and velocity dispersion, then scale B to the dense filament density and calculate Alfven speed, magnetic Mach number, and magnetic energy E_B
key_parameters: delta_V(C18O) = 0.6 km s^-1; n(H2)(C18O) = 1.7 x 10^4 cm^-3; delta_phi = 36.6 deg; sigma_v(filament) = 0.23 km s^-1
assumptions: Q = 0.5; C18O/H2 = 1.7 x 10^-7; depth of C18O region = 0.1 pc; B proportional to rho^kappa with kappa in [0, 2/3], adopting B = 510 uG in the dense filament
